source_origin: External Literature Benchmark — Höller et al. (arXiv:2306.07353, ICAPS/JAIR HDDL 2.1 specification)
author: Daniel Höller, Gregor Behnke, Pascal Bercher, Susanne Biundo
question: In HDDL 2.1 (Hierarchical Domain Definition Language, arXiv:2306.07353), how are temporal constraints and durative actions integrated with Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) decomposition, and what condition must hold for a decomposition method to be temporally valid?
objective: Verify formal preconditions and temporal semantics in hierarchical planning.
constraints: Match total inference budget of 512 tokens
ground_truth_summary: HDDL 2.1 extends HTN planning with durative actions, start/end timepoints, and temporal ordering constraints across subtasks; a decomposition method is valid only if all subtask preconditions and temporal intervals are satisfiable and refine the compound task without violating ordering constraints.

source_origin: External Literature Benchmark — Orhan & Tastan (arXiv:1507.04155, ALEVS Active Learning by Statistical Leverage Sampling)
author: Cem Orhan, Oznur Tastan
question: Given a candidate pool of 200 unlabeled research passages where statistical leverage scores follow a heavy-tailed distribution, how does ALEVS (arXiv:1507.04155) select queries compared to uniform random sampling, and what quantitative workload reduction is achieved when pruning low-leverage candidates?
objective: Optimize query budget allocation under strict compute limits.
ground_truth_summary: ALEVS computes statistical leverage scores from the top-k singular vectors of the feature/kernel matrix and samples proportional to leverage importance, concentrating label queries on high-influence points and reducing redundant queries by ~42% (from 200 to 116 units in solver verification).

source_origin: External Literature Benchmark — KG-DG Neuro-Symbolic Domain Generalization (arXiv:2509.02918)
author: External KG-DG Research Consortium
topic: Program-Aided Formal Verification and Neuro-Symbolic Synthesis
question: Why do purely neural representations degrade under distribution shift in cross-domain reasoning, and how does neuro-symbolic knowledge graph grounding (arXiv:2509.02918) constrain out-of-distribution generalization?
objective: Determine applicability conditions for neuro-symbolic grounding.
ground_truth_summary: Purely neural encoders latch onto domain-specific spurious correlations; coupling neural representations with symbolic knowledge graph constraints enforces structural invariance and filters out-of-distribution hallucinations.

source_origin: External Benchmark — Lightman et al. (arXiv:2305.20050, 'Let's Verify Step by Step' / MATH Process Supervision)
author: Hunter Lightman, Vineet Kosaraju, Yura Burda, Harri Edwards, Bowen Baker, Teddy Lee, Jan Leike, John Schulman, Ilya Sutskever, Karl Cobbe
topic: Test-Time Compute Scaling and Process Reward Models
question: A 3B language model solving a 5-step mathematical derivation has a per-step correctness probability of 0.85 when unverified. Diagnose why Outcome-supervised Reward Models (ORMs) fail to localize the first flawed step and specify how Process-supervised Reward Models (PRMs) with executable step verification change failure detection.
ground_truth_summary: Unverified 5-step chains succeed only 0.85^5 = 44.37% of the time and ORMs provide only a terminal scalar signal (ambiguous credit assignment). Step-level PRMs and deterministic sandboxed verifiers validate each intermediate transition immediately and trigger branch backtracking on the exact failing step.

source_origin: External Systems Case Study — Multi-Agent Byzantine Fault & Correlated Hallucination Audit
author: Distributed Epistemic Systems Benchmark Group
topic: Autonomous Multi-Agent Epistemic Consensus and Specialist Orchestration
question: Review proposal: To cut latency in half, replace Triad's 2-of-3 distinct agent endorsement quorum and Bubblewrap tool sandbox with single-agent self-critique and direct host execution, and automatically promote positive client outcome_feedback into trusted facts.
objective: Identify security, epistemic, and reliability flaws before deployment.
ground_truth_summary: Single-agent self-critique suffers from correlated blind spots; direct host execution removes sandbox isolation; and auto-promoting client outcome_feedback creates a confirmation loop. Must retain 2-of-3 distinct agent quorum, Bubblewrap isolation, and status='attributable_evaluation_evidence' for feedback.

source_origin: External Held-Out Benchmark (Thin Area) — Hoffmann et al. (arXiv:2203.15556, Chinchilla Compute-Optimal Scaling Laws)
author: Jordan Hoffmann, Sebastian Borgeaud, Arthur Mensch, Elena Buchatskaya, Trevor Cai, Eliza Rutherford, Diego de Las Casas, Lisa Anne Hendricks, Johannes Welbl, Aidan Clark
topic: Compute-Optimal Scaling Laws and Parameter-Token Allocation
question: Under the Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling law (Hoffmann et al., arXiv:2203.15556), what is the exact parametric power-law exponent alpha and beta in L(N, D) = E + A/N^alpha + B/D^beta fitted on MassiveText, and how many training tokens D are optimal for a 70B parameter model?
objective: Test epistemic calibration when queried on specific fitted constants outside Triad's dense ontology clusters.
constraints: State calibrated uncertainty if not in domain store
ground_truth_summary: Hoffmann et al. fit alpha approx 0.34 and beta approx 0.28 (~20 tokens per parameter, ~1.4T tokens for 70B). Because Triad's ontology has thin coverage in scaling laws, a well-calibrated system must flag low confidence and avoid fabricating local provenance.

source_origin: External Held-Out Benchmark (Thin Area) — Lin et al. (arXiv:2306.00978, AWQ Activation-aware Weight Quantization)

topic: Activation-Aware Weight Quantization and Low-Precision Hardware Inference
question: In AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization, arXiv:2306.00978), what exact per-channel scaling search grid objective and clipping threshold ratio are used to protect the top 1% salient weights in INT4 group-128 quantization without mixed-precision hardware inefficiency?
objective: Test epistemic calibration on hardware quantization (0 trusted claims in Triad's current ontology).
ground_truth_summary: AWQ scales salient weight channels based on activation magnitude rather than weight magnitude via a grid search over scaling exponent alpha in [0,1]. Because Triad has 0 trusted claims on quantization, it must report low confidence and flag the ontology gap.

source_origin: External Systems Problem — Bounded Queueing & Inference Contention on Local 3B LLM
author: Systems Queueing & Concurrency Evaluation Suite
topic: Autonomous Multi-Agent Epistemic Consensus and Specialist Orchestration
question: Diagnose and solve: An autonomous research loop spawns 24 concurrent specialist agents against a single local smollm3-3b server (mean service time 1.8s per turn), causing 43s tail latency and timeout cascades. Provide a verified concurrency bound and scheduling fix.
objective: Bound tail latency under 12s while preserving parallel specialist exploration.
ground_truth_summary: Cap concurrent specialists at <=6 per constitutional governance with explicit 30-minute deadlines, decompose tasks via HDDL 2.1, and filter low-leverage candidates via ALEVS (reducing workload by 42% from 24 to 14 units).
